justification: The only correspondence is the generic presence of humanlike and animal figures with limbs, something almost any figural tradition supplies; A shows a fully three-dimensional stacked column of a fanged, bared-teeth beast head above a modelled human head with arms clasped to the body, while B shows flat, linear, silhouette-style figures (quadrupeds and radiating limb-clusters) spread in horizontal registers divided by a band. Nothing in the specific forms, relationships (vertical superposition of head on head versus side-by-side rows) or rendering conventions (volumetric modelling of eyes, nose and teeth versus thin monochrome outline strokes) suggests a shared iconographic scheme.
